sections.name: File setup, Link
sections.title: Imports and external link type
sections.what: Brings in the components, styles and helpers the viewer needs, including the 3D scene and panel pieces. It also defines the shape of an external link.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: SceneProject
sections.title: Project record shape
sections.what: Describes one project in the scene: its identifier, category, placement offset and rule, fidelity note, limitations and links.
sections.why: Likely reason: one agreed shape lets the viewer and the data source use the same names.
sections.watch_out: These are compile-time type descriptions only, so mismatched data arriving at runtime is not caught here.

sections.name: SceneAsset
sections.title: Asset record shape
sections.what: Describes one drawn asset: its identifier, owning project, component data, the activities that build it, the activities that only give context, and a limitation note.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping building and context activities separate lets the viewer highlight them differently.
sections.watch_out: Do not merge the two activity lists, since highlighting relies on telling them apart.

sections.name: AliceRecord
sections.title: ALICE record shape
sections.what: Describes one ALICE element: its name and identifier, recipe name if any, mapping status, evidence, unresolved notes, spreadsheet location, candidate schedule activities and source references.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The recipe name may be missing, so code that displays it must handle an empty value.

sections.name: ProgrammeScene, ProgrammePanel
sections.title: Whole scene data shape
sections.what: Defines the full package the view receives: schema and build identities, the schedule, per-project models, projects, assets, review links, ALICE records, source hashes and coverage notes. It also lists the panel names the view supports.
sections.why: Likely reason: one agreed shape keeps the server and the viewer in step.
sections.watch_out: The identity fields name saved viewer settings, so changing how they are produced resets every saved layout.

sections.name: PROGRAMME_DOCK
sections.title: Bottom dock button order
sections.what: Lists the seven panel buttons in the order they appear in the bottom dock, each with its internal name and label.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed order keeps the dock predictable.
sections.watch_out: The internal names must match the names used in panel state, so a rename needs changes in both places.

sections.name: PROGRAMME_PANELS, keyOf
sections.title: Default open panels and key helper
sections.what: Sets which panels start open: layers, checklist, timeline, lifecycle and captions open, while view and inspector start closed. It also reserves dock space and joins a project and activity identifier into one key.
sections.why: Likely reason: the first screen stays uncluttered, and the joined key makes matching quick.
sections.watch_out: The key uses a slash as separator, so an identifier that contains a slash could match the wrong activity.

sections.name: LocalLinks
sections.title: Local-only link filter
sections.what: Shows only links that use plain http and point to this computer, localhost or 127.0.0.1, and opens them in a new tab.
sections.why: Likely reason: review links come from the data, and this limits what the page will open.
sections.watch_out: Other links are dropped without any message, so a missing link may be the rule rather than an error.

sections.name: ProgrammeSceneView (part 1)
sections.title: Scene state and filtered lists
sections.what: Sets up the view's remembered choices, such as filters, date basis, selection, colours and panel state, reusing saved values where present. It then works out which projects, assets and activities match the filters, the schedule's start and end, the chosen date, the active story, and the lists of concurrent activities, relationships and ALICE mappings.
sections.why: Likely reason: many lists depend on the same filters, so they are worked out together from one place.
sections.watch_out: Whenever the basis changes, the date is pulled back into the schedule range, so a saved date can jump.

sections.name: ProgrammeSceneView (part 2)
sections.title: Playback clock and page layout
sections.what: While Play is on, this moves the date forward. In chronological mode it steps the date ahead every 0.2 seconds, and in story mode it moves to the next activity every 1.4 seconds. It also saves the current view settings and works out the status counts and source facts shown for the selected item.
sections.why: Likely reason: playback runs on a timer that must stop and restart as the user's choices change, so the timer is rebuilt whenever its inputs change. Reason for the exact step sizes is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The timer is rebuilt whenever any of its listed inputs change, so adding or removing an input changes when playback restarts.

sections.name: ProgrammeSceneView (part 3)
sections.title: Inspector, view panel and playback bar
sections.what: Holds the right-hand inspector with four tabs. Activity shows searchable activities, their planned and actual dates, and linked source facts. Coverage explains how much of the programme is drawn. Logic lists schedule links. ALICE lists proposed mappings that are not confirmed. The bottom bar has Start, Play and End, the playback mode, the date basis, a date slider and a status summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: the programme holds a lot of detail, so it is split into tabs and the playback controls sit in one bar. The on-screen notes repeat that planned dates are not actual status and that links are not electrical connections.
sections.watch_out: Several on-screen notes say planned is not actual and that links are not electrical connections. Keep those notes when editing, because users rely on them.

sections.name: ProgrammeSceneView (part 4)
sections.title: Closing the page layout
sections.what: Closes the tags that wrap the page, the stage and the footer, and ends the component. It does not change anything the user sees by itself.
sections.why: Structural only. Reason not stated in the code beyond being the normal end of the page.
sections.watch_out: If a closing tag is lost while editing the sections above, the layout breaks for the whole page.

summary: The main viewer for a programme scene: it applies filters, shows the 3D model and timeline, and manages the side panels.
purpose: Lets the owner explore the schedule-based model by date, activity, coverage, logic and ALICE records.
why: Likely reason: the schedule, model and evidence are kept in one view so that filters apply everywhere.
how: Reads saved viewer settings, applies category and project filters, works out dates and matching lists, then shows the dock, the panels and the 3D scene. Only the first 9 of 12 blocks were visible, so the later steps are not described.
inputs: A programme scene, a job identifier and an optional project identifier.
outputs: A 3D model and panels on screen. Viewer settings are saved in browser storage.
risks: Only part of the file was visible. With no dates, the start falls back to 1970, which can show odd dates.
debug: If the view looks empty, check the category and project filters, then whether the scene has dates for the chosen basis.
